stemMd: According to the passage, which of the following is stated about the global average charge for sending 200 dollars?
instructionsMd: Answer on the basis of the passage only.

options.label: A
options.textMd: It has not changed in any market over the past decade, despite the spread of mobile money.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It has fallen below 4 per cent in every corridor, including the intra-African ones.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It is highest in the corridor running from the Gulf states to South Asia, at over 8 per cent.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It is more than twice the 3 per cent target set under the Sustainable Development Goals.

explanationMd:
The third paragraph states the figure directly: the global average charge for sending 200 dollars 'sits at about 6.2 per cent, more than double the 3 per cent target that governments set for themselves under the Sustainable Development Goals'. The option stating that the charge is more than twice the 3 per cent target restates exactly that relationship, and the arithmetic agrees: $2 \times 3 = 6$, and $6.2 > 6$.

**How to work an explicit-information question efficiently.** Locate the sentence that contains the number in the stem, then test each option against that sentence and its immediate neighbours. Do not reason from what seems economically likely — only from what the text says.

The three wrong options each fail on a single word that the passage contradicts or never supplies: *any* market, *every* corridor, and *highest*. Scanning for these absolute quantifiers is the fastest way to eliminate options on this question type.

distractorRationale.a: The passage says prices 'have barely moved in a decade' only 'where that exclusivity holds' — that is, in the particular markets where banks have exclusive agreements with payment networks. This choice removes that condition and generalises to every market, which the passage does not support; indeed it says mobile money has narrowed the gap where it has been allowed to compete, so the 'despite' clause ignores that mobile money is exactly what has moved prices in some markets.
distractorRationale.b: The passage gives 'under 4 per cent' as the cost of one specific kind of corridor, those served by many competing operators. It says in the very next clause that several intra-African corridors exceed 8 per cent, so the claim that every corridor, the intra-African ones included, is below 4 per cent contradicts the text.
distractorRationale.c: This reverses the passage. The Gulf-to-South-Asia corridor is offered as an example of a cheap corridor, under 4 per cent, because many operators compete there. The 'over 8 per cent' figure belongs to several intra-African corridors, the expensive ones the passage names.

accessibilityText: A question about the accompanying prose passage on remittances. It asks which statement about the average charge for sending two hundred dollars is explicitly made in the passage. There is no figure or notation; the answer options are full sentences. They say that the charge: has not changed in any market over the past decade, despite the spread of mobile money; has fallen below 4 per cent in every corridor, including the intra-African ones; is highest in the corridor running from the Gulf states to South Asia, at over 8 per cent; and is more than twice the 3 per cent target set under the Sustainable Development Goals.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The passage says the average of 6.2% is 'more than double the 3 per cent target', which is D. C swaps the corridors (Gulf-South Asia is under 4%, intra-African corridors exceed 8%), B is false, and A distorts the claim about exclusive markets. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-bocconi-verbal-logic-tila-reading-run1) reached the same answer: The passage says the global average is about 6.2%, 'more than double the 3 per cent target'. C is wrong because Gulf to South Asia is under 4%. B is wrong because intra-African corridors exceed 8%. A is wrong because prices barely moved only where exclusivity holds.]
